v.rationale: All three suites pass. All three pass the probes: a PHP file disguised as PDF gets 422, SVG content uploaded as .png gets 422, wrongly typed fields get 422, a non-numeric id gets 404, and an end-to-end Unicode filename download works with nothing written to the public disk. None has a hard functional bug. They all use temporarySignedRoute with 10 minutes, a signed download route outside auth, hashed storage names on the private disk, and 404 for a missing file at both stages. impl-2 ranks first. It is the cleanest idiomatic solution: a policy with denyAsNotFound, an explicit private disk, creation through the relation, thin invokable controllers, original_name used for the attachment, and focused tests that cover the boundaries. impl-3 has the most modern validation (File::types()->max()) and the broadest tests. It drops to second because it relies on the default disk for confidential files, ignores the stored original_name when naming the download, and adds test noise (Http::preventStrayRequests). impl-1 is correct and compact but least idiomatic: inline validation, a hand-rolled strict === ownership check instead of a policy, user_id in fillable, and one test that bundles every validation scenario.
